A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same HPA study, with complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary sections A–E. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison; PDF pages 4–13 render identically.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original HPA benchmark comparisons and ablations. The appendices include calibration-size experiments, performance across training stages, and model-output case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations, calibration-size experiments, stage-wise evaluations, and case studies reported in v1.

M1.justification: The focusing-based parameter partition, balanced parameter selection, and orthogonal parameter adjustment remain unchanged. Section 3 and Algorithm 1 specify the same procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six CVIT datasets, VLGuard and SPA-VL alignment data, and VLG-1, VLG-2, and Ch3EF safety evaluations. Original-data and 0.1% harmful-data-injection scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Zero-shot, DirFT, SeqFT, EWC, Replay, SEFE, Model Tailor, SPPFT, and Safe Delta. Table 3 retains the same SeqFT and Model Tailor comparisons; figure-level comparator membership is also unchanged.

E3.justification: The LLaVA-v1.5-7B backbone, LoRA tuning, task sequences, evaluation metrics, and calibration settings are unchanged. Appendix A and Table 4 retain the same training and test sample counts.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same component ablations, retention-rate and coefficient analyses, task-order tests, parameter-overlap analysis, and case studies. Appendix B–D retains the calibration-size study and stage-wise evaluations without additions or removals.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same point-estimate tables and plots. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted or qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 1 reports HPA AP/MASR of 75.73%/4.75% on Original Data and 76.62%/7.22% with 0.1% Harmful Data Injected in both versions.

T1.justification: The optimization objectives, importance-score definitions, parameter-selection equations, and orthogonal-update derivation are unchanged. The appendix discussion of the relationship between k and p is also identical; no proof or formal assumption is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about post-safety-alignment CVIT, HPA's three components, and balancing safety preservation with task performance. The added code-access statement does not alter these scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the safety–task trade-off, parameter overlap, orthogonal adjustment, and calibration-size effects are unchanged. The constraints concerning access to safety-alignment data and repeated alignment costs remain the same.

D1.justification: v2 adds an HPA GitHub repository address and a code-availability statement to the abstract, absent from v1. This adds access information; implementation details, hyperparameters, and data-processing descriptions remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 40 references and related-work discussion are retained. Positioning relative to prior CVIT and safety-alignment methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract gains one code-availability sentence, and the arXiv version/date margin text changes. The remaining prose, terminology, section organization, and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence causes small changes to column breaks and text positioning across pages 1–3. Figures, tables, captions, and their contents are unchanged; pages 4–13 render identically.

improvement.justification: The new repository address modestly improves reproducibility documentation by telling readers where to find the implementation. Scientific content and supporting evidence remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or executability, so the demonstrated benefit is limited to access information.
